findings.title: Unescaped Referer header is injected into executable JavaScript
findings.body: `request.referer` is interpolated directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string. The controller only verifies the parsed host, but an attacker can send a request with a forged Referer such as `https://<embeddable-host>/?x=';...` and cause arbitrary JavaScript to be emitted and executed under the Discourse origin. Serialize the value for JavaScript (and preferably derive and use only the validated origin) rather than interpolating the raw header.

findings.title: Imported remote HTML bypasses Discourse's sanitizing cook pipeline
findings.body: Posts created by `TopicEmbed.import` use `cook_method: raw_html`, and this branch returns `raw` unchanged. Feed content and readability-extracted page content are external, attacker-controlled HTML; `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative links and does not sanitize tags, event handlers, scripts, or dangerous URL schemes. The resulting `post.cooked` is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and can also be rendered in normal topic views, allowing a compromised feed/article source to execute script in forum visitors' browsers.

findings.title: postMessage is sent to a full Referer URL instead of an origin
findings.body: The second argument to `postMessage` must match the recipient's origin. `request.referer` normally includes the embedded page's path and query (for example `https://example.com/article`), so it does not equal the parent origin `https://example.com` and browsers will reject or fail to deliver the resize message. As a result, the iframe commonly remains at its default height. Build a scheme/host/port origin from the validated Referer before passing it to `postMessage`.

findings.title: Message-origin validation accepts prefix origins
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` treats any origin string that is a substring/prefix of the configured Discourse URL as trusted. For example, with `https://forum.example.com/`, an origin such as `https://forum.example.co` passes this test. An untrusted frame can therefore send `discourse-resize` messages and set the Discourse iframe to an arbitrary height. Parse `discourseUrl` and compare `e.origin` for exact origin equality.
